pr_title: Fix results screen pushed after rewinding in-between push delay
pr_body:
Closes #8793 

Although the issue is talking about the results screen pushed with current score after rewinding, as I've proposed in the thread, it's kind of annoying to push the results screen after rewinding from completion (by accident for example), so I've decided to solve this by cancelling the push delegate instead which technically solves this.

## Remarks
 - I wasn't initially sure about this solution but given that the `Player` push the results screen when all hit objects have been judged, this will do for now.

issue_context.title: rewinding replay as soon as it ends may result in incorrect result screen score
issue_context.body:
When the replay ends, if you try to rewind the replay it shows a result screen with incorrect score

The final score should be 1000000 but it's not.
https://streamable.com/zawmoz

osu!lazer 2020.418.0
comments: I feel like the best behaviour to this would be to cancel pushing results screen if the replay didn't rewind during the delay between the completion and push time, will look into fixing this.

review_comments:
seems like this could use old value to prevent redundant checks?
```suggestion
            if (completionState.OldValue && !completionState.NewValue)
```

using `OldValue` in bool events is redundant here as I haven't used `BindValueChanged(..., true)` which makes `NewValue` always the opposite of `OldValue`, therefore not adding anything.

btw the operations done inside this block is required to make the cancellation correct (hopefully), as they all reset everything that was set when a completion occurs:
 - `completionProgressDelegate?.Cancel()` – cancel the completion delegate to prevent from pushing. the delegate may already be null, so add a null-conditional, due to `allowResults` being false, thus not creating the delegate.
 - `completionProgressDelegate = null` – reset the delegate back to null to assure the `Player` that there isn't a push delegate scheduled.
- `ValidForResume = true;` – Reset back `ValidForResume` from being false to allow pausing back (though just remembered that rewinding comes only on replays which you can't pause, but to ensure that there are no traces of the player going through the completion process.)
Fair point about the old value being redundant, although there was no need to explain the rest as it was pretty obvious even to me what it did.
